web_evidence.title: Crossroads of Twilight
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained Chapter 1 excerpt consistently narrates Mat, Noal, and Egeanin as he or she while presenting Mat's memories and perceptions without a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Crossroads of Twilight Literary Elements
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies the book's narrator and point of view as a third-party narrative.

web_evidence.title: Crossroads of Twilight Book by Robert Jordan (Wheel of Time, #10)
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly records the novel's POV as third person with multiple viewpoint characters.

web_evidence.title: Revisiting the Wheel of Time: Crossroads of Twilight
web_evidence.note: A systematic whole-book reread maps the prologue, every chapter, and the epilogue to named character POVs such as Mat, Perrin, Elayne, Egwene, and Rand, corroborating a shifting limited-POV structure rather than an alternate narratorial strand.

person_note: The base narration is third person with limited focalization shifting among many characters. The authorized opening renders Mat and others in third person, while the Goodreads interior passages q00969, q00970, and q00972 independently expose the same nonparticipating narratorial position. Whole-book POV sources describe third-person, multiple-view narration and map the viewpoint shifts across all sections. Generic 'you' passages are aphoristic or focalized generalizations, direct-speech pronouns are local, and q00953's 'we' belongs to an embedded poem; none constitutes a sustained first- or second-person base section. No credible contrary structure was found.
